title: GPU compute seam: a headless compute crate with capability probe, CPU fallback and one parity-tested kernel (facet binning)

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P4
labels.description: Work the maintainer asked for, for the next cut

body:
Part of #2526 (GPU shader toolpath generation). Slice 2 of 5. Needs slice 1 (#2619) for the CPU reference.

Maintainer order (2026-11-18): "GPU shader issues get priority". Thus this issue is `P4`.

## Why
Only `camcraft-ui` links wgpu today, through the `egui_wgpu::wgpu` re-export (`Cargo.toml` lines 46-47). The generators run in `camcraft-app` and `camcraft-motion`, and in the CLI and MCP with no window. They have no GPU access. The headless device policy exists, but in `crates/ui/src/headless_gpu.rs`.

## What
- A new crate (recommended name `camcraft-gpu`) for headless compute. It holds:
  - The device policy of `headless_gpu.rs` (software adapter first in tests, then hardware), moved down from `camcraft-ui`. `camcraft-ui` then uses it.
  - A capability probe: `DownlevelFlags::COMPUTE_SHADERS`, `max_storage_buffer_binding_size`, `max_compute_workgroup_storage_size`. WebGL2 and GL below ES 3.1 have no compute: the probe says "no compute" by name.
  - One device for each process, made on the first request and cached (`OnceLock`). Never made for each operation or each frame.
  - A switch to turn the GPU off (recommended: `CAMCRAFT_GPU_COMPUTE=off`) for tests and for machines with bad drivers (#2424, #74).
  - One kernel: conservative facet binning. Input: facet boxes in tile-relative f32, padded by `r` plus a margin. Output: the cell lists.
- The CPU path runs, with the same result, when there is no adapter, the probe fails, the device is lost, or a buffer is past the limit. The log names the reason one time. Never a panic, never `unwrap` on a GPU future.

## Pinning tests (CPU reference)
- Superset parity: for the same facets, each facet in the CPU grid cell of #2619 is in the GPU cell list. Extra GPU entries are permitted.
- Refusals: a buffer past the limit, and a forced "no compute" probe, give `Err` with the reason. The caller uses the CPU grid.
- Adapter policy: the `headless_gpu` rule (#615). No adapter prints a loud SKIP. `CAMCRAFT_REQUIRE_GPU=1` turns the skip into a failure. The self-hosted runners have the Mesa software drivers (`runners` skill), so the lane runs on lavapipe there.

## Decision entry and dependencies
- A `docs/decisions/` entry is necessary: new crate edges (`camcraft-ui` and `camcraft-app` onto the new crate). The entry lists the imported items and what rebuilds.
- A direct `wgpu` dependency is new for the workspace. The version must be the one that the egui set pins (`=30.0.1` with egui-wgpu `=0.36.2`), so no second wgpu enters the lock. The review sets `needs-maintainer` for this dependency, by AGENTS.md.
- The wgpu version then moves with the egui set (#658, #1118). The decision entry says so.
- `camcraft-motion` gets no GPU dependency. The app computes the GPU result and passes it into motion as a value.

Effort: `effort:high` (several crates, new behaviour with its tests). No posted output changes in this slice.

Done means: the new crate exists with the probe, the cached device, the CPU fallback and the binning kernel; the superset parity test passes on the software adapter; `camcraft-ui` uses the moved device policy; the decision entry is in the PR.
